newsitem.title: USA: Point Beach 2, Wisc. nuke in mechanical difficulty.
newsitem.headline: Point Beach 2, Wisc. nuke in mechanical difficulty.

text.p: Wisconsin Electric Power Co said its 485 megawatt (MW) Point Beach 2 nuclear power unit is experiencing mechanical difficulties prior to a planned restart from a refueling outage later this week.
"We are looking at some additional issues with a seal in a reactor coolant pump," a company spokesman said.
The spokesman declined to give any further information on the status of the unit or any possible delay to its restart.
Wisconsin Electric, a subsidiary of Milwaukee-based Wisconsin Energy Corp, plans to issue a statement on the status of the unit later today, the spokesman said.
The company had been expecting the unit to begin electricity production late this week and reach full power late next week.
The unit, in Two Rivers, Wisconsin, has been shut since October, 1996 for refueling and maintenance.

Point Beach 2 was in a hot shutdown mode and was "cooling down to mode 5 for leaking reactor coolant pump seal replacement," the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said in its daily plant status report for Thursday.
The NRC said a restart date for the unit was not known.
The adjacent 485 MW Point Beach 1 nuclear unit had been expected to begin electricity production two to three weeks after unit 2 reached full production.
Point Beach 1 has been shut since February 18 for maintenance.
